Raj — thanks for the call earlier. Attaching the draft order form we have (latest internal), and a one-page summary of the commercial schedule. Before we route to legal, a few quick clarifying asks from Finance/Sales so we can prioritize redlines: 

- Net terms: can you confirm Stellix is asking for Net45 (per today’s note) vs Net30? Our standard is Net30. If Net45, is that company policy or tied to PO internal approvals?
- Invoicing cadence: we typically invoice monthly in arrears for usage, with an upfront minimum-credit invoice — is that OK or do you need staged invoices tied to milestones?
- Taxes: your comment about reverse-charge in the EU — can you confirm Stellix will provide VAT IDs and SIRET/Tax IDs for each entity we invoice? Who will be the invoice remittance entity?
- Withholding: any withholding expected on payments to Redwood (US entity)? If so, percentage and citation would help our tax team.

Please also attach the PO and redlines if you have them (we’ll put legal on any wording changes to MSA/Order Form). I’ve cc’d Emma so we can see the PO when you share.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Legal and Sales ops once we have the PO + redlines.

— Lauren

Lauren — thanks, attaching our PO and a tracked-redline version of the OF. Quick answers below and a couple asks from our side: 

- Net terms: Stellix policy is Net45 for new vendor relationships above $50k ARR; Net30 considered after 6 months (we can provide written policy).
- Invoicing cadence: prefer monthly invoices; we would like an initial invoice that covers the first 30 days as a deposit if possible.
- Taxes: for EU entities we expect to apply reverse-charge when applicable. We will provide VAT IDs but need Redwood to accept reverse-charge where local law permits.
- Withholding: not expected for our US entity. Some of our AP teams in Spain/DE may withhold; we will flag if applicable and share citations.

Attachments: Stellix_PO_7891.pdf; Stellix_redlines.docx — legal has made a few minor MSA wording suggestions (mainly around liability cap and data processing references). Thanks for the summary, Lauren. I reviewed the redline and my counsel below — high level: acceptable commercially with a few contract-level protections we should insist on. 

Key legal asks / recommended counter points:
- Net terms: commercial concession to Net45 for first 6 months is acceptable. Contract should explicitly state the reversion to Net30 after a 6-month review and provide an invoicing schedule example.
- Reverse-charge / VAT: we will accept reverse-charge treatment only where Stellix provides a valid VAT registration and the invoice is issued to the corresponding VAT-registered entity. Add clause: "Customer shall provide valid VAT registration numbers and supporting documentation prior to invoicing; absent valid documentation Redwood may charge VAT and seek recovery."
- Withholding: require specificity. Insert a clause stating that any withholding must be supported by local law and Customer must provide documentation. If withholding is applied, Customer will provide prompt evidence and Redwood can gross-up or issue a tax credit note as applicable.
- Liability / DPA changes: the redline edits to liability cap are acceptable provided we retain the carveback for gross negligence and third-party claims. For DPA items, route to Privacy counsel — we may accept the data processing tweak if an addendum clarifies processor/subprocessor list.
- Minimum commit / invoicing: redline the order form schedule to call out the invoice split (e.g., "Initial deposit invoice for first 30 days = $X; Monthly usage invoices thereafter in arrears"). If Stellix wants invoices split across legal entities, we need the exact remit-to entity names and tax IDs before countersigning.

Please see attached "Redwood_redline_summary.pdf" for tracked recommendations. Finance: can you confirm whether Net45 for first 6 months is allowable and sign-off on invoice routing? Sales — if we accept Net45 initially, do we need to adjust pricing or require a smaller initial commit?

— Kimberly

Agree with Kimberly’s approach. Proposing a commercial compromise to get this over the line: 

- Offer Net45 for the first 6 months (no price change) with a contractual reversion to Net30 at month 7. Include an explicit review clause at month 5 to confirm payment performance.
- Accept EU reverse-charge where Stellix provides VAT IDs per-entity and we invoice the matching entity; otherwise Redwood will charge VAT.
- For the initial deposit: invoice 30 days up-front for the minimum commit. Finance to confirm routing details (PO number and AP contact required on invoice).
- Minimum-commit phasing: allow a 2-tranche split across entities only if Stellix provides entity names, tax IDs and confirms remittance for each tranche in writing.

If Legal signs off on Kimberly’s drafted clauses I’m good to send the counter. I’ve prepared a countersigned order form (Redwood_Counter_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with the Net45 concession and the VAT language included. Suggest we send that along with a short cover email and the DocuSign link.

Happy to take the sync with Stellix if needed — recommend 20 minutes to walk procurement through routing and tax evidence.

— Ben
